findings.title: Readiness does not enforce the fallback required by its CI-independence result
findings.trigger: A fork or non-owner, non-bot PR changes .github/ and readiness receives a complete inspection record for the same head/base, with no fallback. Such evidence can be reused from an exempt same-repository bot PR at the same commit, or retained across a policy upgrade.
findings.execution_path: runCli recomputes ciDefinitionsChanged. readiness marks CI ready as not-independent, but does not pass that requirement into codexStatusFor. The latter accepts a complete inspection record without consulting fallback. The final aggregation explicitly accepts not-independent, returning ready: true.
findings.consequence: The checklist announces readiness to request approval despite the documented requirement for an owner-approved fallback on this PR.
findings.evidence: A direct call with isCrossRepository=true, ciDefinitionsChanged=true, internally bound complete inspection evidence and fallback=null returned ready=true, CI ready=not-independent and Codex=ok. All 12 targeted existing tests passed. The 'ready only through the owner-approved fallback' test starts with an incomplete status; the CLI test at lines 1463–1473 checks display text but does not assert readiness is blocked.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the independently computed CI-independence requirement constrain the Codex acceptance decision. A complete inspection record must not satisfy that item when the current PR requires fallback. Add regressions with complete evidence and no fallback for fork and non-bot collaborator PRs, including evidence reused from an exempt bot PR.
